annotations.description: Fetching Mountain instead of Island is a significant mistake. The player's hand contains Back to Basics, Flame of Anor, Dress Down, and Swords to Plowshares. Back to Basics requires UUU-heavy mana and punishes nonbasic lands - it's the key card against the opponent's Underground Sea / Badlands mana base. Having a basic Island would provide blue mana for Back to Basics (which costs 2U), Dress Down (1U), and Flame of Anor (1UR). The player already has Tundra for white mana (Swords to Plowshares). Getting a Mountain only helps cast Flame of Anor's red requirement, but an Island is far more important since the player needs UU or more blue sources for their key spells, and importantly, fetching Island means they can cast Back to Basics on turn 3 with Tundra + Island + Prismatic Vista (if they play it), while still being able to untap all their lands since they'd all be basics (except Tundra which taps for U). With Mountain, they have a harder time casting their blue-heavy spells and Back to Basics specifically.
annotations.betterLine: Fetch Island to support casting Back to Basics on turn 3 (the most impactful card in hand against opponent's nonbasic-heavy mana base) and to better support the blue-heavy spell suite (Dress Down, Flame of Anor's draw mode)

annotations.description: With the opponent tapped out and Force of Negation already in the graveyard, this was the perfect window to execute the LED + Beseech the Mirror combo. Play Verdant Catacombs, fetch a land, cast Beseech the Mirror, hold priority to crack LED (discarding hand doesn't matter since Beseech is on the stack), and sacrifice LED as Bargain to cast any CMC ≤4 card for free. Instead, Brainstorm was cast, which delays the combo and gives the opponent time to find answers.

annotations.description: Grk41F Humble used Force of Will's alternative cost (pay 1 life + exile a blue card) to counter Thoughtseize when they had 7 untapped lands (Mountain + 6 Islands), more than enough to hardcast it for {3}{U}{U}. This unnecessarily costs 1 life and a blue card from hand.
annotations.actionTaken: Used Force of Will's alternative cost, exiling a blue card and paying 1 life
annotations.betterLine: Hardcast Force of Will for {3}{U}{U} using the available untapped lands, preserving the blue card in hand (likely Dress Down or the second Force of Will) and 1 life point

annotations.description: With two Swords to Plowshares already in hand and the opponent having zero creatures on the battlefield (and key threats in exile), taking a third Swords to Plowshares over Brainstorm is suboptimal. Brainstorm provides crucial card selection to find threats or answers, and is far more impactful in this board state where the game needs to be closed out.
annotations.actionTaken: Selected Swords to Plowshares from Thundertrap Trainer's trigger despite already having two copies in hand and no opposing creatures.
annotations.betterLine: Select Brainstorm, which provides card selection to dig for win conditions like additional Forth Eorlingas! or more countermagic to maintain the lock.

annotations.description: Grk41F Humble's only white source is Tundra, which is locked down by their own Back to Basics enchantment. With only Mountain and Islands untapped, they cannot produce the {W} required by Forth Eorlingas! at any X value. Additionally, even if W were available, X=4 requires 6 total mana but they only have 5 untapped lands. They should be holding up Force of Will to protect against the opponent's combo pieces (LEDs, Chrome Mox, Mox Opal still on board) rather than tapping out for a spell they may struggle to cast properly.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Forth Eorlingas! with X=4, likely unable to produce the required white mana due to Back to Basics locking Tundra.
annotations.betterLine: Pass the turn holding up Force of Will and reactive spells, or if wanting to deploy threats, ensure mana base can support the cast. Consider destroying own Back to Basics via Prismatic Ending to unlock Tundra if white mana is critically needed.

annotations.description: Failed to crack Lion's Eye Diamonds in response to their own Thoughtseize on the stack. With the opponent completely tapped out (no counterspells possible), cracking both LEDs would discard Echo of Eons to graveyard and generate 6 mana (e.g., 3U+3U). Then Echo of Eons could be flashed back for 2U, drawing 7 fresh cards with 3 mana still floating plus Mox Opal and Chrome Mox on battlefield. This is the classic Storm line and likely wins the game on the spot.
annotations.actionTaken: Passed priority without activating Lion's Eye Diamonds, allowing Thoughtseize to resolve normally while keeping Echo of Eons stranded in hand.
annotations.betterLine: With Thoughtseize on the stack, activate both Lion's Eye Diamonds (discarding hand including Echo of Eons), float 6 mana (e.g., 3U+3U), let Thoughtseize resolve to see opponent's hand, then flashback Echo of Eons for 2U with 3 mana remaining and artifacts in play to storm off.

annotations.description: Gem3F Vet is at 7 life facing lethal from 8 attacking creatures next turn. They have two untapped Lion's Eye Diamonds and Echo of Eons in hand. They can activate both LEDs (discarding Echo of Eons to graveyard), generating 6 mana, then flashback Echo of Eons for {2}{U} to draw 7 fresh cards with 3 mana still floating. This is their only realistic path to survival, and the opponent is completely tapped out with no ability to counter.
annotations.actionTaken: Passed without casting anything, effectively conceding to the lethal attack next turn.
annotations.betterLine: Activate both Lion's Eye Diamonds (discarding hand, putting Echo of Eons in graveyard), then flashback Echo of Eons for {2}{U}. With 3 mana floating and 7 fresh cards, attempt to combo off or find answers to survive.
